summary: The first Cascumpeque light was lit on Sandy Island in 1854. Its 1876 tower stands, privately owned, after the light was deactivated in 2004 and its 1968 successor removed in 2005.

light.note: The 1876 tower has been inactive since 1970 (Rowlett) or since 1968 (LighthouseFriends, which says the old tower was sold when the new light went up). Deactivation of the 1968 light: January 2004 (LighthouseFriends) or after the December 2004 storm (Rowlett, who gives 'inactive since 2004').

range_lights.note: Two range towers on the sand hills south of the entrance, 1900; discontinued May 1901 and moved to Sandy Island, lit 11 July 1901 (Marine reports FY1900 and FY1901). Separate structures from the main light.

structures.type: square wood pyramidal tower with lantern and gallery, attached to a two-storey keeper's house
structures.note: LighthouseFriends gives 12.5 m (41 ft); Rowlett gives about 15 m (49 ft). Moved to the south side of the entrance in 1899. Privately owned.

structures.type: square skeleton tower with lantern and gallery
structures.note: 17 m (58 ft) per Rowlett. Deactivated 2004; demolished June 2005; light not replaced (Rowlett). LighthouseFriends: metal tower removed from the site in 2005.

staffing.note: LighthouseFriends lists keepers to 1967 (Wilfred Richard Gaudin, 1944-1967). The de-staffing date is not in the sources read.

access.note: Privately owned. Grounds, dwelling and tower closed (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett). Accessible only by boat (Rowlett).

visit.note: Rowlett: visible from the Northport Range Rear Light.

events.note: Put into operation on Sandy Island at the harbour entrance, the year after the 1853 petition (LighthouseFriends); Rowlett: station established 1854
Combination lighthouse and dwelling, and range light, built by James Keefe for $1,900 (LighthouseFriends)
Gale of 29 October 1879 washed the front range light off its foundation and damaged the tower (LighthouseFriends)
Brush and stone erosion protection placed on Sandy Island in 1889 and 1890 (LighthouseFriends)

Moved 2,280 feet south across the harbour entrance in the winter of 1899, at a cost of $576.72, supervised by Milton Walsh (LighthouseFriends); the 1876 tower moved to the south side in 1899 (Rowlett)
Range masts replaced by two towers on the sand hills south of the entrance; buildings erected for $183 under Milton Walsh's supervision (Marine report FY1900)
Range lights discontinued in May 1901; buildings moved to Sandy Island and lit 11 July 1901 (Marine report FY1901)
New square skeleton light put into operation near the old tower in October 1968 (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett)
Old 1876 tower sold to a group of Charlottetown residents, who used it as a vacation retreat (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett). Names not recorded.
Sandy site damaged by a winter storm; light deactivated, January 2004 (LighthouseFriends). Rowlett dates the damaging storm to December 2004.
Modern tower demolished in June 2005; light not replaced (Rowlett). LighthouseFriends: metal tower removed in 2005.

corrections.why: The light was deactivated in January 2004 (LighthouseFriends) and has been inactive since 2004 (Rowlett). Its 1968 successor was demolished in 2005 and not replaced (Rowlett). The 1876 tower has been inactive since 1970 (Rowlett).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1876 and Rowlett's 1854 are both right for different towers. 1854 is the station's first light on Sandy Island (LighthouseFriends: put into operation 1854). 1876 is the tower built by James Keefe, which is the one standing now. The first tower was replaced in 1856 by John Smallwood.

notes_for_editor: 1) Spelling: the Marine reports (to 1924) use 'Cascumpec'; LighthouseFriends says a 1966 attempt standardised 'Cascumpeque'. The story uses Cascumpeque and says Cascumpec in the reports. 2) Status: the record's 'active' (OSM) conflicts with LighthouseFriends and Rowlett (deactivated 2004). Proposed correction above. 3) 1968 vs 1970: LighthouseFriends says the old tower was sold when the modern light went up in 1968; Rowlett says the old tower has been inactive since 1970. Stated as LighthouseFriends' 1968 sale; not resolved. 4) The storm that damaged the site: January 2004 (LighthouseFriends, which dates the deactivation) against December 2004 (Rowlett, which dates the storm). The story gives both. 5) Tower height of 1876 tower: 12.5 m (LighthouseFriends) against about 15 m (Rowlett). Stated in the text. 6) Keepers: the list is LighthouseFriends' throughout. Tuplin (1897) was checked against the 1911 keeper list, scan p.255 (printed p.253): the page image shows the row 'Sandy Island, (Cascumpec) | Jas. C. Tuplin | May 5, 1897 | 360 00' in one line. The station name does not say main light or range lights; LighthouseFriends ties Tuplin to the main light. The story says so. Mallet and Mallett are not treated as one person; LighthouseFriends' overlapping years for Mallet, Mallett, Perry and Gaudin are stated in the text. 7) The range-light masts: the FY1900 report (scan p.75) says masts; LighthouseFriends dates mast lights on Savage Island to 1897, moved to Cascumpec in 1899. Not resolved; the story says only that masts were replaced by towers. 8) Private owners of the 1876 tower are not named (private residents of a converted lighthouse). 9) The LighthouseFriends access note offers a pontoon trip with a named contact; omitted. 10) The 1900 range-light sentences and the $183 cost are cited to scan p.76 (printed p.61), not p.75; the FY1901 move to Sandy Island is scan p.82. 11) Record coordinates (46.798706, -64.036807, OSM) and focal height 18 m were not checked against any source read here.
